title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-09
content:
Daily scratchpad - experiment notes, quick run logs, and todos

Date: 2026-03-09
Owner: Asha Patel
Context: follow-up on quantized model evals (gptq 4-bit) for latency/cost tradeoff on small-chat workloads. Quick notes to capture runs and next steps before pairing with Maya.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Finish systematic prompt set for safety/regression checks (10 prompts per category)
- [ ] Re-run teacher-student eval with seed 42 across 3 quant configs (8-bit, 4-bit-gptq, 4-bit-awq)
- [ ] Add timing hooks to batching harness to break down queue vs decode latency
- [ ] Validate tokenizer consistency for specialized prompts (emoji + code blocks)
- [ ] Create short readme + benchmark snippet for console team

Quick experiment log (local GPU - p4d):
1) run: eval_prompts.py --model rwi-small-v1 --quant gptq-4 --seed 42 --batch 4 --stream false
   notes: successful; first pass; outputs look OK but few hallucinations on code snippets
   perf: avg_latency_per_request=210ms, tokens/sec=280, mem=10.8GB
   quality (quick): pass@1-like metric on retrieval-chat set = 0.62 (baseline fp16=0.67)

2) run: eval_prompts.py --model rwi-small-v1 --quant awq-4 --seed 42 --batch 4
   notes: slightly lower quality; repeated tokenization mismatch on backticks; need to check token offsets
   perf: avg_latency=190ms, tokens/sec=310, mem=9.6GB
   quality quick = 0.58

3) run (8-bit): eval_prompts.py --model rwi-small-v1 --quant int8 --batch 4
   perf: avg_latency=220ms, tokens/sec=260, mem=11.2GB
   quality quick = 0.66

Initial interpretation: gptq-4 gives the best quality/latency balance so far but we need more systematic evals and more seeds. AWQ looks promising for throughput but has tokenization edge cases. 8-bit preserves quality but uses slightly more memory and is slower in this setup.

Prompt set notes:
- categories: casual-chat, instruction-following, multi-turn-reasoning (3-turns), code-generation (short snippets), safety (toxic/edge cases)
- create 10 canonical prompts per category; include variants with emojis, markdown, and inline code fences
- seed list: [42, 123, 999] for reproducibility
- scoring: exact-match for code, BLEU and human-like heuristics for chat, and safety classifier flags for safety set

Quantization & infra notes:
- GPTQ pipeline used: https://github.com/ichuang/gptq (local fork with small-fix for layernorm ordering)
- AWQ binary from internal artifact (awq-build v0.9) - need to add version pin to experiment metadata
- Watch out: tokenizer offsets cause AWQ outputs to shift on multi-token punctuation (backticks, triple-dash). Suspect difference in decode rounding - check kv-cache alignment test
- Suggest adding a small unit test: feed prompt with repeated backticks and compare token positions between fp16 and quantized runs

Metrics capture plan:
- Save per-request latencies (queue + decode) to s3 path: s3://rwi-eval/applied-ml/2026-03-09/<run>-metrics.csv
- Save outputs and prompt pairs to s3 path for later human evals
- Add automated pass/fail rules: if code-pass@1 drops >0.05 vs baseline, mark regression and block rollout

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is our baseline for rwi-small-v1 set to fp16 on p4d? (I think yes, check run history)
- Should we include a 2-bit async quant run? risky but worth exploratory test on dev pool next week
- How does batching policy interact with prefix KV-cache reuse in these models? Need to trigger same prefix multiple times to measure caching effects

Next steps (short):
- Re-run all three quant configs with seeds [42,123,999] and batch sizes [1,4,8] on infra/dev-quant queue (Jordan to reserve nodes)
- Add tokenizer unit test for backtick/code fence edge cases (me)
- Write a 1-pager summarizing perf vs quality tradeoffs for Console team (due 2026-03-12)

Random notes / scratch commands:
- quick diff command: python -c "import json; x=json.load(open('out_fp16.json')); y=json.load(open('out_gptq4.json')); print(sum(1 for a,b in zip(x,y) if a['resp']!=b['resp']))"
- profile hook: export RW_EVAL_PROFILE=1 && python eval_prompts.py --profile_out profile.pb

Hand-off to Maya/Jordan: will sync tomorrow 10:30 to go through results, confirm node reservations, and align on safety prompt set.
